findings.checklist_item: Add an acceptance criterion that verifies each of the three call sites retains its distinct exception surface (push.py: except OSError with %r log; drain/sweep: except Exception with exc_info=True), e.g. a source-level or unit assertion over the caller except clauses.
evidence: Plan: 'the three sites do not catch identically (push.py catches only OSError, logging %r; drain/sweep catch broad Exception with exc_info=True) and folding the catch into the helper would silently broaden push.py's exposure'
Plan: 'so the refactor changes no exception surface' — asserted but no AC maps to it
AC1 verifies 'none re-implements the bootstrap or the detach flags'; AC2 is a static scan for detach tokens/bootstrap — neither checks the per-caller except clauses
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'the refactor changes no exception surface' and that each caller keeps its existing except clause and log line, but no acceptance criterion verifies this preservation. AC1-AC3 verify only that the bootstrap/detach-flags live solely in _proc; a homogenized or folded catch would satisfy them.
findings.location: Scope bullet 1 ('it RE-RAISES on failure — the never-raise posture stays per-caller') and Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: Executor consolidates spawn logic and inadvertently moves the try/except into the helper, silently broadening push.py from OSError-only to broad Exception — all AC still pass green
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: 'Each of the three call sites keeps its pre-refactor except clause and log line (push.py catches OSError logging %r; enrich_drain and compact_trigger catch Exception with exc_info=True) — verified by unit tests that assert the helper re-raises and that each caller swallows-and-logs its own way.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavioral test asserting spawn_detached returns a child env that preserves the caller-provided projection (push.py's secret-stripped env survives PYTHONPATH layering; caller keys are not overwritten by the bootstrap).
evidence: "the helper only layers the PYTHONPATH bootstrap onto whatever env the caller provides, so consolidation cannot drop push.py's secret-stripping"
AC #2 is a static source scan; AC #5 relies on CI pytest green but names no env-layering assertion
The env-layering point is the one materially NEW integration behavior the helper introduces (each caller previously constructed the full child env itself)
findings.finding: The plan states an invariant that the helper 'only layers the PYTHONPATH bootstrap onto whatever env the caller provides, so consolidation cannot drop push.py's secret-stripping' but names no behavioral test asserting the layered child env preserves the caller's secret-stripped projection (push.py's `project_child_env(relationship="unrelated")` + `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`). The static source-scan (AC #2) and the migrated Windows detach-kwargs test do not cover env layering.
findings.location: Scope bullet 1 ('the helper only layers the PYTHONPATH bootstrap onto whatever env the caller provides') and Acceptance Criteria #2/#5
scenarios: A future edit to spawn_detached that inadvertently reorders env layering (e.g. bootstrap dict overwriting caller keys, or vice versa) drops push.py's secret-stripping and no test catches it — the exact silent-broadening the plan says it prevents
findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit test that calls spawn_detached with a sentinel caller env (including a would-be-stripped secret key set to a marker and REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always) and asserts the resulting child env still contains the caller's values plus only the PYTHONPATH bootstrap layered on top.

findings.checklist_item: Enumerate the detached-spawn test consumers whose monkeypatch seam the refactor relocates (at minimum tests/unit/test_detached_child_cwd.py, tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py:856, tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py:547) and state how each is re-pointed at the _proc seam.
evidence: Plan names only 'tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py::test_windows_detach_kwargs (and any other direct caller of a per-site _detach_kwargs)'

tests/unit/test_detached_child_cwd.py calls _spawn_detached_drain/_spawn_detached_sweep/push_tickets_branch and its _Recorder captures the Popen kwargs (cwd, start_new_session/creationflags) at the per-site call
tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py:850-861 patches `D.subprocess` (module-local) then calls `D._spawn_detached_drain(wt)` and asserts `argv[3]`/`kwargs['cwd']`
tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py:542-551 patches `compact_trigger.subprocess` (module-local) then calls `_spawn_detached_sweep(wt)` and asserts the argv
findings.finding: The test-migration scope enumerates only test_windows_detach_kwargs and callers of a per-site _detach_kwargs, but omits the detached-cwd/Popen test consumers whose monkeypatch seam the refactor breaks.
findings.location: Scope bullet: 'Test consumers of the per-site helpers move with them'
scenarios: After the Popen call moves into _proc.spawn_detached, patching compact_trigger.subprocess or enrich_drain.subprocess no longer intercepts the spawn, so the argv/cwd assertions in these tests silently stop exercising the real call and fail (or pass vacuously)
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the test-migration bullet: these tests patch the per-site module's local `subprocess`/inspect per-site Popen kwargs; after consolidation they must patch `rebar._proc`'s Popen seam (or the helper must call through a monkeypatchable `_proc.subprocess`) so the cwd/argv/detach-flag assertions keep exercising the real spawn.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether the repo_root cwd-fallback change (if 'change') should be a separate child ticket, since it targets long-lived in-process callers distinct from the three detached-spawn sites being consolidated here.
evidence: "the three detached children no longer reach it now that they get an explicit cwd. But the exposure survives for long-lived IN-PROCESS work, which cannot be given its own cwd"
The in-process callers (daemon threads at _mcp_writes.py:575, editor.py:523, janitor.py:440, _heartbeat.py:69, reconciler) are a different concern than the detached-spawn consolidation
This is advisory-only diffusion — surfaced, not prescribed; the decision is coupled to the same cwd root cause
findings.finding: AC #4 bundles a decision affecting a materially different consumer set — long-lived IN-PROCESS callers (5 named daemon threads / reconciler across _mcp_writes, workflow/editor, _snapshot/janitor, _heartbeat, config) that cannot be given an explicit cwd — into a ticket whose core outcome is consolidating the three DETACHED-child spawn sites. If the recorded decision is 'change', implementing a degraded repo_root fallback touches those unrelated subsystems and is independently valuable/releasable from the spawn-site consolidation.
findings.location: Scope bullet 4 and Acceptance Criteria #4 ('recorded decision (accept or change) on repo_root's cwd fallback for long-lived in-process callers')
scenarios: If the decision is 'change', the in-process degraded-fallback implementation is a distinct, testable, releasable increment (different callers, different failure mode) that could ship independently of the helper consolidation

tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py monkeypatches `_spawn_detached_drain` by name at lines 230,254,266,296,319,331,344,357,371
tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py:106 monkeypatches `_spawn_detached_sweep` by name

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the spawn_detached interface enumeration to name the per-site child ARGV (the positional args threaded into the -c stub tail) and the cwd-anchor path, since push threads [base_path, src]/cwd=detached_child_cwd(base_path) while drain/sweep thread [canonical_tracker, src]/cwd=detached_child_cwd(tracker).
evidence: push.py passes argv [base_path, src] and its stub reads sys.argv[1] as the tracker; enrich_drain/compact_trigger pass [_canonical_tracker(tracker), src]
push.py anchors cwd=detached_child_cwd(base_path); drain and sweep anchor cwd=detached_child_cwd(tracker) — different source path per site
The plan lists only 'the child entry point, their stderr sink, and their child ENV' as caller-supplied, so the helper's interface does not obviously accommodate the varying argv/cwd-anchor
findings.finding: The Scope's enumeration of caller-supplied inputs to spawn_detached omits two inputs that materially differ across the three call sites: the per-site child ARGV threaded into the -c stub, and which path anchors the durable cwd.
findings.location: Scope bullet 1 ('Callers would supply the child entry point, their stderr sink, and their child ENV')
scenarios: Implementer designs spawn_detached with a fixed argv shape and cannot reproduce push's [base_path, src] versus drain/sweep's [canonical_tracker, src] without rework
Helper hard-codes the cwd anchor to a single parameter name and the push site (base_path) or drain/sweep (tracker) can no longer thread its own anchor
findings.suggested_fix: State that spawn_detached accepts the caller's entry-point import+call tail plus the caller's positional argv, and a cwd-anchor path (base_path for push, tracker for drain/sweep) from which the helper derives cwd via detached_child_cwd; the helper owns only the 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[N]); ' bootstrap prefix and the appended src slot.
